title: Shard-aware worklet executor and backpressure protocol cleanup
creator: Ava Chen
description: Replace the current monolithic consumer loop with a shard-aware 'worklet' executor that schedules bounded execution slices per shard, simplifies retry semantics, and standardizes backpressure signals across Redis and Kafka connectors. Goal: reduce head-of-line blocking, improve tail latency under mixed-priority traffic, and make retry behavior auditable and configurable.
acceptance_criteria: New worklet executor is live behind feature flag for Redis and Kafka consumers
P90 token latency for multi-tenant burst tests reduced by >=20% vs baseline
No increase in duplicate-delivery rate beyond existing thresholds (<=0.5%)
Retry multiplier and idempotency policy configurable per topic/stream in runtime config
Observability: per-shard active worklet count, retry-window histogram, and H-o-L stall metric available in Grafana
implementation_steps: Design: define "worklet" (max execution time, resource budget, acknowledgment semantics) and per-shard scheduling policy
Prototype: implement executor patch for Redis Streams consumer group using XAUTOCLAIM-based lease reconciliation
Adapter: implement equivalent small-slice execution on Kafka consumer (pause/resume per-partition with timed worklets)
Retry: centralize retry multipliers into a shared policy service and wire into both connectors
Backpressure: introduce a bounded local inflight queue + dynamic token-bucket per-shard; expose shed/queue metrics
Observability: add metrics and traces; wire to existing rollout dashboard and add alert for long-running worklets
Gradual rollout: feature flag -> small % of tenants -> monitor -> widen -> flip default
Docs & runbook: migration notes, debugging steps for worker stalls, and rollback instructions
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ava Chen: Initial writeup and spike completed. Prototype shows simpler lease reconciliation for Redis using XAUTOCLAIM reduces stolen work rate in 1k-shard test.

2026-02-23 - Riley Kapoor: Reviewed prototype. Key concerns: how do we ensure Kafka pause/resume granularity doesn't cause consumer group rebalances? Proposed using pause windows < poll timeout and aggressive cooperative rebalancing on partition ownership changes.

2026-03-01 - Design review (with Priya, Marco): Agreed on worklet max execution of 150ms for CPU-bound tasks; IO-heavy tasks can opt-in to longer slice via 'long-worklet' flag. Need explicit contract in SDK about ack semantics.

2026-03-04 - Spike results: microbench against existing consumer under mixed priorities (50% high-prio short tasks, 50% long tasks) shows 28% improvement in P95 latency and 35% drop in observed head-of-line stall events.

2026-03-07 - Engineering sync: Decided to centralize retry policy into runtime-config with fields: base_backoff_ms, max_attempts, idempotency_hint, and backoff_multiplier. This lets ops tune per-tenant without deploy.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8423 - worklet executor, Redis adapter. Requesting review from @marco and @selene
2026-03-10 - QA note: Found a race when converting inflight map to shard buckets during consumer restart. Riley to add deterministic handoff unit tests and fix double-ack scenario.
